# Lab 23.4: Failover Drill: Soft vs Hard Failover

## What We Are Going to Do
Run a planned soft failover, measure the recovery point, fail back, then delete the paid resources.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Write a marker row and note the time.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">INSERT INTO lab23_dr.orders VALUES (999999, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP());
SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() AS before_failover;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Start a soft failover.** **Disaster recovery → lab-dr → Failover → Soft failover**. A soft failover waits until all data is replicated, so nothing is lost. A **hard** failover switches immediately and may lose the most recent writes; you use it only during a real outage.

3. **[SQL] Check after failover.** Run in `us-east4`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT MAX(order_id) AS last_order FROM lab23_dr.orders;   -- 999999 is there

SELECT replica_name, replica_primary_assigned, replication_time
FROM `region-us-east4`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA_REPLICAS
WHERE schema_name = 'lab23_dr';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   `replication_time` tells you the recovery point (RPO).

4. **[Console] Fail back.** Run another soft failover so `us-central1` is primary again.

5. **[CLI] Delete everything.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --location=us-central1 \
  "ALTER SCHEMA lab23_dr SET OPTIONS (failover_reservation = NULL); DROP SCHEMA lab23_dr CASCADE"
for A in $(bq ls --reservation_assignment --location=us-central1 --format=json | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(a['name']) for a in json.load(sys.stdin)]"); do bq rm --reservation_assignment $A; done
bq rm --reservation --location=us-central1 lab-dr</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Soft failover | No data loss, used for drills |
| Hard failover | Immediate, may lose recent writes |
| RPO | From `replication_time` |
| Clean-up | Reservation and replica deleted |
